title: Expressing emotions
summary: Two words for love (mahál and ibig) and when to use each, and saying what you like with gustó and ibig
goals: Know the meanings of mahál and ibig and their verbs mahalín and ibigin
Say I love you and talk about loving family, friends and country
Choose mahál for family love and ibig for love between a man and a woman
Say what you like or love to do with gustó or ibig + a ligature
Use gustóng-gusto for a strong liking

blocks.t: The English *to love* has two rather different meanings in Tagalog, shown by the verbs **mahalín** and **ibigin**. Their root words are **mahál** and **ibig**.

head: Root
Verb
What the root means
rows: Literally *noble* and *expensive*. As a term of endearment: *dear* or *beloved*. It suggests that someone **values** something or someone.
*A fondness for someone or something*. It can also mean *affection, desire, purpose, whim* and *love*, from the simple (a whim) to the complex (love).
blocks.title: Mahál and ibig

blocks.t: A word made from mahál is **mahalága**, which means *important*.

items.tl: Dápat náting mahalín ang áting báyan.
Minámahál ko ang áking mga magúlang.
Minámahál niyá ang kanyáng bunsô nang higít sa lahát.
items.en: He/She loves his/her youngest child the most.

blocks.title: Spot the pattern
blocks.t: In these examples **minámahál** (loves) is followed by the one who loves, in the possessive form: *Minámahál **ko*** (I love), *Minámahál **niyá*** (he/she loves), *Minámahál **nilá*** (they love). The one who is loved comes after **ang**.

For **sensual love between a man and a woman**, use **ibig**. The feelings a man and a woman share are called **pag-iíbígan** (*mutual love*), and they have **pag-ibig** (*love*) for each other. A weaker term, which still suggests strong affection, is **pagmamáhálan** (*bond of love*).

For the **filial love** between a parent and a child, between siblings, between friends, and in all other kinds of relationships, the forms of **mahál** are used instead. So either **pagmamahál** or **pagmamáhálan** (both meaning *love*) is used.

head: Relationship
Use
Words
rows: Parent and child, siblings, friends, all others

Meaning
blocks.title: Love in the family uses mahál
Love of country
blocks.t: The exception is the poetic and patriotic use of the noun **pag-íbig** for love of one's country: **pag-ibig sa tinubúang lúpa**. Filipino heroes Dr. Jose Rizal and Andres Bonifacio used it in their writings for their fellowmen in the late 19th century.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Romantic love between a man and a woman: ibig (pag-ibig, pag-iíbígan).
Family, friends and everyone else: mahál (minámahál, pagmamahál, pagmamáhálan).
Love of country: pag-ibig sa tinubúang lúpa.

blocks.t: *To like* shows fondness for someone, or for doing certain activities. The Tagalog equivalent is **gustó** or **ibig**, and the two can be used **interchangeably**.

blocks.title: Linking rules with gustó and ibig
items: The ligatures **-ng** or **-g** are attached to possessive pronouns such as **niyá**, **ko** and **namín**: niyá**ng**, ko**ng**, namín**g**.
The possessive word **ni** (or **ng**, see Lesson 8) and the ligature **na** follow the usual rules: *Gustó ni Tom **na** basahin…*
**si** comes before a name such as Claudette, **siná** if the noun is plural.
**ng** comes before the name of a thing, and **sa** before the name of a place.

blocks.title: Gustó + doer + ligature + action
blocks.note: Gustó kong maglúto. / Gustó ni Tom na basahin ang libró.

items.en: He/She loves to swim. (The book adds: or ibig.)
We love to walk in the rain.
I love to read before going to bed.

items.tl: Gustó ni Tom na basahin ang libró.
items.en: Tom likes to read the book.

blocks.t: **Gustó** can be doubled, as in **gustóng-gusto**, to show an **intense feeling or desire** for something or someone.

exercises.q: What are the two root words for "to love"?
exercises.explain: The verbs are mahalín and ibigin.

exercises.q: What does mahál literally mean?
exercises.explain: As a term of endearment it means dear or beloved.

exercises.q: Which word made from mahál means "important"?
exercises.explain: Mahalága = important.

exercises.q: Which root can also mean affection, desire, purpose and whim?
exercises.explain: Ibig is a fondness for someone or something.

exercises.q: "Mahál kitá" means…
exercises.explain: Mahál kitá.

exercises.q: Which word do you use for sensual love between a man and a woman?
exercises.explain: They have pag-ibig for each other.

exercises.q: Which word do you use for love between a parent and a child?
exercises.explain: Filial love uses the forms of mahál.

exercises.q: Which sentence is proper for "I love my child"?
exercises.explain: Love for a child uses mahál.

exercises.q: What does pag-iíbígan mean?
exercises.explain: The feelings a man and a woman share.

exercises.q: What does pagmamáhálan mean?
exercises.explain: A weaker term that still suggests strong affection.

exercises.q: "Pag-ibig sa tinubúang lúpa" is…
exercises.explain: The poetic and patriotic exception, used by Rizal and Bonifacio.

exercises.q: Which two words both mean "to like" and can be swapped?
exercises.explain: They may be used interchangeably.

exercises.q: Fill in: Gustó ___ maglúto. (I love to cook.)
exercises.explain: Add -ng to ko before the verb.

exercises.q: Fill in: Gustó ni Tom ___ basahin ang libró.
exercises.explain: After a name, the ligature na is used.

exercises.q: Fill in: Gustó ko ___ Claudette.
exercises.explain: Si comes before a name.

exercises.q: Fill in: Gustó nilá ___ Tagaytay. (They like Tagaytay.)
exercises.explain: Sa comes before the name of a place.

exercises.q: What does gustóng-gusto show?
exercises.explain: Gustó is doubled.

recap: Mahál (noble, expensive; dear, beloved) and ibig (fondness, affection, desire, love) both give verbs for to love: mahalín, ibigin.
Romantic love between a man and a woman: ibig (pag-ibig, pag-iíbígan).
Family, friends and all other love: mahál (Minámahál ko ang áking anák; pagmamahál, pagmamáhálan).
Love of country is the exception: pag-ibig sa tinubúang lúpa.
To like: gustó or ibig + pronoun with -ng/-g: Gustó kong maglúto. Gustóng-gusto = like very much.
